title: Score every cut with one sorted pass
brief: Write the weighted gain of a split, list the cuts worth trying on one feature, and find the best split with running sums.
hints: split_gain weights each child by its share of the rows: node_impurity(y, criterion) - (n_left * I_left + n_right * I_right) / n. On y = [1, 3, 8, 10] with the first two rows on the left, the answer is 13.25 - 1 = 12.25.

candidate_thresholds sorts x, takes 0.5 * (xs[:-1] + xs[1:]), and keeps position i only when xs[i] != xs[i + 1] and both sides hold at least min_samples_leaf rows. The left side of position i has i + 1 rows.

In best_split, np.searchsorted(xs, thresholds, side='right') gives the left count for each threshold. Index the cumulative sums with n_left - 1. Subtract y.mean() from y first when the criterion is mse.
